Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Look up the order via `tidectl orders show <id>`: if both charges share the same idempotency key it's a single real charge plus an authorization that auto-expires in 7 days (no action needed), but if the keys differ it's a genuine duplicate — check `payment_events`/webhook logs and refund the extra charge from the Paylane dashboard, opening a bug if it's our fault.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Run `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1` to apply the paired `.down.sql` and undo the last migration; if it dropped or rewrote data (the down file can't restore that), instead do a point-in-time Postgres restore to before the migration via the WAL-G recovery procedure.

Certificates auto-renew via certbot with a DNS challenge on a systemd timer every 12 hours (Let's Encrypt certs last 90 days, renewed every 60); if that fails, the manual fallback is `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on `kelp-1`, then rebuild the HAProxy bundle (`haproxy-cert-bundle`), `systemctl reload haproxy`, and verify with `curl -vI https://tidewater.example`.

Sources: tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md

TLS certificates renew automatically via a certbot systemd timer running every 12 hours (using DNS challenge), with a deploy hook that rebuilds the HAProxy cert bundle and reloads it without dropping connections, plus an alert if a cert is within 14 days of expiry. If automatic renewal fails, the manual fallback on `kelp-1` is: `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`, then rebuild the HAProxy bundle (`haproxy-cert-bundle`) and `systemctl reload haproxy`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md
